wiki_text: In September 2025 the Delaware River Basin Commission granted a second five-year extension of the Gibbstown LNG export terminal's construction permit; the Delaware Riverkeeper Network filed a federal lawsuit in November 2025 challenging the extension. Construction has not begun. The project's viability is clouded by parent New Fortress Energy's 2025-2026 debt restructuring (NFE negotiated a plan in March 2026 to avoid Chapter 11) and by the loss of its planned LNG feedgas: the affiliated New Fortress Wyalusing liquefaction plant was cancelled in July 2025 and the company's LNG-by-rail permit lapsed, removing the dock's intended supply chain.

As of February 2026 the Penn LNG export project in Chester, Pennsylvania was reported dead: sponsor Penn America Energy had been dissolved and the project never secured contractors, feed gas, permits, financing, or buyers. A successor effort associated with the same principal (Franc James) is reportedly pursuing a site in neighboring Eddystone, PA under a new Delaware-registered entity, 'Eddystone Energy LLC,' engaging in NDAs with state/local bodies; no permits had been filed as of early 2026.
